get.summary: Downloads files as ZIP file with optionally increasing the download counter
get.description: This API call downloads multiple file that are not expired and increasing their download counter is disabled by default. Can be set up to return a pre-signed URL instead of the zip file itself, which is valid for 30 seconds and can be accessed by any registered user. End-to-end encrypted files and encrypted files stored on cloud servers cannot be downloaded. Returns 404 if an invalid/expired ID was passed. Requires API permission DOWNLOAD. To download files that were not uploaded by the user, the user needs to have the user permission LIST

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: IDs of files to be downloaded seperated by comma

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: The filename for the new Zip file. If the filename includes non-ANSI characters, you can encode them with base64, by adding 'base64:' at the beginning, e.g. 'base64:ZmlsZW5hbWU='

parameters.name: increaseCounter
parameters.description: Increase counter if set to true

parameters.name: presignUrl
parameters.description: Return a pre-signed URL instead of the actual file. Valid for one download within 30 seconds and can only be used by logged in users. When this option is set, download counter cannot be increased.

400.description: Invalid input or trying to download an end-to-end encrypted file

401.description: Invalid API key provided for authentication or API key does not have the required permission

404.description: Invalid ID provided or file has expired

To download files that were not uploaded by the user, the user needs to have the user permission LIST

post.description: Uploads a file in chunks, in case a reverse proxy does not support upload of larger files. Parallel uploading is supported. Must call /chunk/complete after all chunks have been uploaded. WARNING: Does not support end-to-end encryption! If server is setup to utilise end-to-end encryption, file will be stored in plain-text! To upload an end-to-end encrypted file, use gokapi-cli. Chunks must be at least 5MB in size, unless last chunk of file. Requires API permission UPLOAD

401.description: Invalid API key provided for authentication or API key does not have the required permission

post.description: Needs to be called after all chunks have been uploaded. Adds the uploaded file to Gokapi. Requires API permission UPLOAD

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The unique ID that was used for the uploaded chunks

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: The filename of the uploaded file. If the filename includes non-ANSI characters, you can encode them with base64, by adding 'base64:' at the beginning, e.g. 'base64:ZmlsZW5hbWU='

parameters.name: filesize
parameters.description: The total filesize of the uploaded file in bytes

parameters.name: contenttype
parameters.description: The MIME content type. If empty, application/octet-stream will be used.

parameters.name: allowedDownloads
parameters.description: How many downloads are allowed. Default of 1 will be used if empty. Unlimited if 0 is passed.

parameters.name: expiryDays
parameters.description: How many days the file will be stored. Default of 14 will be used if empty. Unlimited if 0 is passed. Ignored if expiryTimestamp is also passed and non-zero.

parameters.name: expiryTimestamp
parameters.description: An absolute Unix timestamp for the file's expiry, e.g. picked from a date/time control. Takes precedence over expiryDays if non-zero. Must not be in the past. Either header is clamped to the server's configured maximum expiry, if one is set.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Sets the password for this file. Omit this header entirely for no password protection. If the header is present, its value is trimmed and must meet the server's minimum password length or the request is rejected with 400; an empty value is NOT treated as 'no password' and is rejected the same way. A password containing bytes outside printable ASCII (or one that happens to start with the literal text 'base64:') should be sent base64-encoded with a 'base64:' prefix, e.g. 'base64:ZmlsZW5hbWU=' - the server decodes it before hashing. Gokapi's own web UI always does this for you.

parameters.name: generatedpassword
parameters.description: Signals that the password header was generated client-side rather than typed by the uploader. Only meaningful together with a non-empty password header. Currently informational only: when the server has StoreShareKeys enabled, the password is stored encrypted with the server master key whether it was generated or typed so it can be retrieved later via GET /files/{id}/sharekey.

parameters.name: nonblocking
parameters.description: If set to true, the call returns without waiting for the file processing to finish.

parameters.name: bundleid
parameters.description: The bundle ID to add this file to. If empty, the file will not be added to any bundle.

parameters.name: recipients
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of email addresses. When non-empty, creating the file (or adding it to the bundle named by bundleid) and restricting it to exactly these recipients happen as one atomic operation: if the grants cannot be created, the whole upload is refused and nothing is left reachable. A bundle is restricted once, at whichever member file's completion call first finds it unrestricted; later member files sent with the same list are a no-op once the bundle already carries the restriction, so recipients are not re-mailed once per member. See POST /share/recipients for the underlying grant mechanics.

400.description: Invalid input, or the recipients header contains an address that could not be validated

401.description: Invalid API key provided for authentication or API key does not have the required permission

412.description: recipients was non-empty but no mail connector is configured, so the access links could not be delivered and the upload was refused

post.summary: Requests a UUID for uploading a new file for a file request
post.description: Requests an UUID that can be used for uplading a new file. The chunks for the new file have to use this UUID. The first chunk needs to be uploaded latest 4 minutes after requesting the UUID. Requires API key associated with the file request. If the file request is restricted to named recipients, the API key alone is not sufficient: the caller must also present that recipient's identity, either the share access cookie or the access token as a sharetoken header or token query parameter. A caller who is not currently on the recipient list is answered as if the file request did not exist.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The file request ID

400.description: Invalid ID or the file request does not accept any more files

401.description: Invalid API key provided for authentication or API key does not have the required permission

404.description: No file request exists with the given ID, or it is restricted to named recipients and the caller is not one of them

429.description: If too many chunks are currently requested, the caller has to wait a couple of seconds and try again. The rate limit now also applies to file requests with a MaxFiles cap, not only to unlimited ones.

post.summary: Frees a reserved UUID if upload was cancelled
post.description: This call frees a reserved UUID, so that it does not count towards the quota anymore. Used if an upload was cancelled or failed. Requires API key associated with the file request. If the file request is restricted to named recipients, the API key alone is not sufficient: the caller must also present that recipient's identity, either the share access cookie or the access token as a sharetoken header or token query parameter. A caller who is not currently on the recipient list is answered as if the file request did not exist.

Please note: This method does not use chunking, therefore if you are behind a reverse proxy or have a provider that limits upload filesizes, this might not work for bigger files (e.g. Cloudflare). Requires API permission UPLOAD

post.description: This API call duplicates an existing file with new parameters. Requires API permission UPLOAD. To duplicate files that were not uploaded by the user, the user needs to have the user permission LIST

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of file to be duplicated

parameters.name: allowedDownloads
parameters.description: How many downloads are allowed. Original value from web interface will be used if empty. Unlimited if 0 is passed.

parameters.name: expiryDays
parameters.description: How many days the file will be stored. Original value from web interface will be used if empty. Unlimited if 0 is passed.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Sets a new password for the duplicated file. Omit this header entirely to keep the source file's original password (protected or not). If the header is present, its value is trimmed and must meet the server's minimum password length or the request is rejected with 400; an empty value is NOT treated as 'no password' and is rejected the same way. A password containing bytes outside printable ASCII (or one that happens to start with the literal text 'base64:') should be sent base64-encoded with a 'base64:' prefix, e.g. 'base64:ZmlsZW5hbWU=' - the server decodes it before hashing. Gokapi's own web UI always does this for you.

put.summary: Changes parameters of an uploaded file
put.description: This API call changes parameters of an uploaded file. Requires API permission EDIT. To edit files that were not uploaded by the user, the user needs to have the user permission EDIT

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of file to be edited

parameters.name: allowedDownloads
parameters.description: How many remaining downloads are allowed. Unlimited if 0 is passed.

parameters.name: expiryTimestamp
parameters.description: Unix timestamp of the file expiration date. 0 is unlimited only if the server has no configured maximum expiry (GOKAPI_MAX_EXPIRY); if a maximum is set, the value is clamped to it instead.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Sets a new password for this file. Omit this header entirely to leave the file's current password protection untouched - this is the only way to edit other fields (e.g. allowedDownloads) without affecting the password. If the header is present, its value is trimmed and must meet the server's minimum password length (GET /api/auth/info, field minPasswordLength) or the request is rejected with 400; an empty value is NOT treated as 'no password' and is rejected the same way. To remove password protection, use removePassword instead of sending an empty password. A password containing bytes outside printable ASCII (or one that happens to start with the literal text 'base64:') should be sent base64-encoded with a 'base64:' prefix, e.g. 'base64:ZmlsZW5hbWU=' - the server decodes it before hashing. Gokapi's own web UI always does this for you.

parameters.name: generatedpassword
parameters.description: Set to true when the supplied password was generated by the client rather than typed by the user. Only meaningful together with the password header. Currently informational only: when the server is configured to store share keys, the password is kept in recoverable form for GET /files/{id}/sharekey whether it was generated or typed.

parameters.name: removePassword
parameters.description: Set to true to remove password protection from the file. This is the only way to remove a password: omitting the password header keeps the current password unchanged, it does not remove it. Cannot be combined with the password header in the same request; doing so is rejected with 400.

400.description: Invalid ID supplied or incorrect data type sent

put.description: This API replaces the content of an uploaded file with the content of a different (already uplaoded) file. Note: Replacing end-to-end ecrypted files is NOT possible and will result in an error. Requires API permission REPLACE. To replace a file that was not uploaded by the user, the user needs to have the user permission REPLACE_OTHERS. To replace a file with the content uploaded by another user, the user needs to have the user permission LIST. To delete a file after replacing, the API key requires the permission DELETE. To delete a file that does not belong to the user, the user needs to have the permission DELETE_OTHER_FILES.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of file to be replaced

parameters.name: idNewContent
parameters.description: ID of the file with the new content

parameters.name: deleteNewFile
parameters.description: If true, the file with the ID passed in idNewContent will be deleted afterwards

400.description: Invalid ID supplied or incorrect data type sent

delete.description: This API call deletes the selected file. If the file's content still exists, it is disposed of (removed from storage) while its metadata record is kept as owner-visible history until the configured metadata retention window elapses; if the file was already disposed of (e.g. previously expired), its history record is removed immediately instead. Deletion can be postponed with the parameter delay, to be able to cancel it with the call /files/restore before the content is disposed of. Requires API permission DELETE. To delete a file that was not uploaded by the user, the user needs to have the user permission DELETE

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the file to be deleted

parameters.name: delay
parameters.description: The number of seconds to wait before deleting the file, in order to be able to restore it with /files/restore

401.description: Invalid API key provided for authentication or API key does not have the required permission

404.description: Invalid ID supplied

post.summary: Restores a file that is pending to be deleted
post.description: This API call cancels a pending deletion of the selected file that was originally deleted with /files/delete. The call to restore has to be within the timeframe specified in the delay parameter of /files/delete, and before the file's content has actually been disposed of - once disposed (for any reason: the pending deletion went through, or the file separately expired or ran out of downloads), it can no longer be restored. Requires API permission DELETE. To delete a file that was not uploaded by the user, the user needs to have the user permission DELETE

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the file to be restored

401.description: Invalid API key provided for authentication or API key does not have the required permission

404.description: Invalid ID supplied, or the file's content has already been disposed of and can no longer be restored

post.description: This API call creates a new file bundle (folder) owned by the calling user. Requires API permission UPLOAD

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the folder. If the name includes non-ANSI characters, you can encode them with base64, by adding 'base64:' at the beginning, e.g. 'base64:ZmlsZW5hbWU='

parameters.name: allowedDownloads
parameters.description: How many downloads this folder allows. One download is spent per visit - fetching the whole zip or any single member counts once, regardless of how many files that visit touches. Unlimited if 0 is passed, or if the header is omitted entirely.

parameters.name: expiryTimestamp
parameters.description: Unix timestamp of the folder's expiration date. Unlimited if 0 is passed, or if the header is omitted entirely, unless the server has a configured maximum expiry (GOKAPI_MAX_EXPIRY), in which case the value is clamped to it.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Sets a password for this folder. Gates every member uniformly - a member's own password, if any, is ignored while it belongs to a folder. Omit this header entirely to create an unprotected folder. If present, its value is trimmed and must meet the server's minimum password length (GET /api/auth/info, field minPasswordLength) or the request is rejected with 400. A password containing bytes outside printable ASCII (or one that happens to start with the literal text 'base64:') should be sent base64-encoded with a 'base64:' prefix, e.g. 'base64:ZmlsZW5hbWU=' - the server decodes it before hashing.

parameters.name: generatedpassword
parameters.description: Set to true when the supplied password was generated by the client rather than typed by the user. Only meaningful together with the password header. Currently informational only: when the server is configured to store share keys, the password is kept in recoverable form for GET /folder/{id}/sharekey whether it was generated or typed.

deletedat.description: Unix timestamp the folder was deleted by its owner, or 0 while it is live. A deleted folder keeps its entry, and its member files keep theirs, until the metadata retention period elapses and both are removed together. It can no longer be opened through its link.

401.description: Invalid API key provided for authentication or API key does not have the required permission

get.description: This API call returns a list of file bundles owned by the calling user. Admin users with LIST_OTHER_UPLOADS permission can see all bundles. Requires API permission VIEW

expireat.description: Unix timestamp the folder itself expires. A member's own expiry is inert while it belongs to a folder - this is the value that governs it.

downloadsremaining.description: The folder's own download allowance. One visit - the whole zip, or any single member - spends one, regardless of how many files that visit touches.

deletedat.description: Unix timestamp the folder was deleted by its owner, or 0 while it is live. A deleted folder keeps its entry, and its member files keep theirs, until the metadata retention period elapses and both are removed together. It can no longer be opened through its link.

membercount.description: Number of member files this bundle still has rows for, including files pending deletion and files whose content has already been disposed of (expired or download allowance exhausted). Those rows remain in a file listing as history for the metadata retention period, with a status saying the content is gone, so the folder summarising them counts the same rows. This is the listing view and is NOT what a recipient would receive.

ispasswordprotected.description: True if the folder is password protected. Only the fact is published, never the hash. A file carries the equivalent as IsPasswordProtected.

totalsizebytes.description: Combined size in bytes of the files counted in membercount, using each row's recorded size. A disposed member keeps its recorded size here, matching the size the file listing shows for that same row; the member status, not this figure, is what says whether the bytes are still stored.

401.description: Invalid API key provided for authentication or API key does not have the required permission

post.summary: Deletes a file bundle/folder and all associated files
post.description: This API call deletes a file bundle and all files associated with it. The folder can no longer be opened through its link from the moment it is deleted. The bundle and its member files stay listed as history, marked deleted, until GOKAPI_METADATA_RETENTION elapses and both are removed together - or until the owner deletes the folder a second time, which removes that history immediately. That mirrors a file, where a second delete purges the retained record the same way; the audit log is the durable record of what happened, not this listing. To delete a bundle of a different user, the user requires the user permission DELETE to execute this call. Requires API permission DELETE

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The folder/bundle to be deleted

401.description: Invalid API key provided for authentication or API key does not have the required permission

404.description: Folder not found

put.summary: Changes the settings of a file bundle/folder
put.description: This API call changes the name, password, expiry and download allowance of a file bundle (folder). A folder owns these settings for every file in it - a member file's own password, expiry and download allowance are inert, which is why PUT /files/modify refuses to change them on a bundled file and points here instead. To edit a folder of a different user, the user needs the user permission EDIT. Requires API permission EDIT

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The folder/bundle to be edited

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Renames the folder. Omit this header entirely to leave the current name untouched. An empty value is rejected with 400, as is a name longer than 256 characters. If the name includes non-ANSI characters, you can encode them with base64, by adding 'base64:' at the beginning, e.g. 'base64:ZmlsZW5hbWU='

parameters.name: allowedDownloads
parameters.description: How many remaining downloads this folder allows. One download is spent per visit - fetching the whole zip or any single member counts once, regardless of how many files that visit touches. Unlimited if 0 is passed. Omit this header entirely to leave the current allowance untouched.

parameters.name: expiryTimestamp
parameters.description: Unix timestamp of the folder's expiration date. Omit this header entirely to leave the current expiry untouched. 0 is unlimited only if the server has no configured maximum expiry (GOKAPI_MAX_EXPIRY); if a maximum is set, the value is clamped to it instead. Every member file that would otherwise be disposed of before the folder expires has its own retention extended to match, so an extended folder still has files in it when the new date arrives.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Sets a new password for this folder. Gates every member uniformly - a member's own password, if any, is ignored while it belongs to a folder. Omit this header entirely to leave the folder's current password protection untouched - this is the only way to edit other fields (e.g. allowedDownloads) without affecting the password. If the header is present, its value is trimmed and must meet the server's minimum password length (GET /api/auth/info, field minPasswordLength) or the request is rejected with 400; an empty value is NOT treated as 'no password' and is rejected the same way. To remove password protection, use removePassword instead of sending an empty password. A password containing bytes outside printable ASCII (or one that happens to start with the literal text 'base64:') should be sent base64-encoded with a 'base64:' prefix, e.g. 'base64:ZmlsZW5hbWU=' - the server decodes it before hashing.

parameters.name: generatedpassword
parameters.description: Set to true when the supplied password was generated by the client rather than typed by the user. Only meaningful together with the password header. Currently informational only: when the server is configured to store share keys, the password is kept in recoverable form for GET /folder/{id}/sharekey whether it was generated or typed.

parameters.name: removePassword
parameters.description: Set to true to remove password protection from the folder. This is the only way to remove a password: omitting the password header keeps the current password unchanged, it does not remove it. Cannot be combined with the password header in the same request; doing so is rejected with 400.

deletedat.description: Unix timestamp the folder was deleted by its owner, or 0 while it is live. A deleted folder keeps its entry, and its member files keep theirs, until the metadata retention period elapses and both are removed together. It can no longer be opened through its link.

get.summary: Get the stored share password for a folder
get.description: Returns the decrypted share password stored for a bundle (folder), if the server has StoreShareKeys enabled and one was actually stored for it (populated from the password of the first member file uploaded into it that had one, typed or generated). Requires API permission VIEW; to view a folder owned by another user, the caller also needs the user permission LIST. Every refusal - unknown ID, no permission, feature disabled, nothing stored - answers identically with 404, so the response cannot be used to probe which of those applies. A sealed instance is the one deliberate exception: it answers 503 so an administrator can tell 'try again after unsealing' apart from 'there was never a key here'.

If resetPassword is "true" and generateNewPassword is also "true", the current password is replaced with a generated one. The caller may never modify themselves, the super admin, or a user whose rank does not sit strictly below their own. Requires API permission MANAGE_USERS

post.summary: Shares a resource with a list of email addresses
post.description: Sets the recipient list of a file, folder or file request to exactly the addresses given. Each address is resolved to an external share recipient, created if unknown, and is emailed a personal access link. An address that is already on the list keeps the grant it holds, so the downloads it has already spent, the allowance it was granted and the time it last collected the resource all survive the edit; an address that is left out of the list is revoked immediately, and adding it again later grants it afresh. Passing an empty list clears the recipient list, returning the resource to anonymous link access. Requires API permission EDIT. To change a resource that was not uploaded by the user, the user needs the user permission EDIT. Returns 412 if no mail connector is configured, since an access link could then not be delivered and the share would be unreachable.

resourceId.description: The ID of the resource being shared

emails.description: The addresses allowed to access the resource. An empty array clears the list

downloadsAllowed.description: Per-recipient download allowance, spent against this recipient alone. 0 takes the resource's own download limit, so the owner's one number applies to each recipient separately - a file limited to three downloads and shared with three people is nine - and only a resource that is itself unlimited yields an unlimited grant. Applies to the addresses this call adds; an address already on the list keeps the allowance it was granted with

get.description: Returns one entry per file, folder or file request the caller may list that has named recipients, each with the addresses it is shared with and how much of their individual download allowance they have used. Resources shared by link only are omitted. Requires API permission VIEW.

get.summary: Lists shares granted to the caller
get.description: Returns every file, folder or file request currently reachable through a share grant whose recipient email matches the caller's own account name. Derived live from the grant rows each call - there is no separate inbox table - so it reflects a grant, a cleared list or a blocked recipient immediately. A grant is skipped if its resource no longer exists, if a file is disposed or past its own expiry, if a file request is closed or past its expiry, or if the recipient has spent their own download allowance and the download window that spending it opened has closed. An account whose name is not an email address, or one that is blocked as a share recipient, gets an empty list. Requires API permission VIEW.

post.summary: Opens a share from the caller's inbox
post.description: Verifies the caller's own email is granted access to the resource, then issues the same recipient access cookie a mailed share link would have exchanged for - no new access token is created, so the link already sitting in the recipient's mailbox keeps working unchanged. Returns the resource's public URL, which the client should navigate to directly so the cookie just set is sent with the request. Requires API permission DOWNLOAD.
